title: Vetala Story 4: The Prince Who Married His Own Sister's Daughter?
summary: The Vetala chuckled: 'O King! Listen to this tangled tale of royal blood and kinship!'...
keywords: vetala story 4: the prince who married his own sister's daughter?
full_text:
King Vikramaditya marched back to the shispa tree, cut down the corpse, hoisted it across his shoulders, and resumed his silent march through the darkness.

The Vetala chuckled: 'O King! Listen to this tangled tale of royal blood and kinship!'

In a southern kingdom reigned King Chandrasena, who had a valiant son named Prince Suryamukha. During a hunting expedition in the mountain borders, the prince was separated from his retinue and found shelter in a remote forest hermitage.

There dwelt an ancient, saintly hermit who had raised an orphaned maiden of celestial beauty named Hemalata. The prince fell deeply in love with her, and with the hermit's blessing, they were wed according to the Gandharva rites.

Years passed, and the prince brought his bride to the royal capital.

It happened that twenty years earlier, during a civil war in the kingdom, King Chandrasena's elder sister had been lost in the forest. Unknown to the king, that lost sister had taken shelter in the mountains, given birth to a daughter, and passed away, leaving her infant girl to be raised by the solitary hermit—the very Hemalata whom the young prince had wed!

When the ancient hermit visited the capital to bless the royal grandchild, he revealed the secret lineage: Hemalata was none other than the daughter of King Chandrasena's long-lost sister!

Thus, Prince Suryamukha had unknowingly married his own father's sister's daughter—his first cousin!

A daughter was born of their marriage, named Priyadarshini.

The royal genealogists and legal scholars gathered in the palace assembly, arguing fiercely over the precise kinship of the newborn child: some claimed she was the prince's niece; some claimed she was his cousin; others claimed she was his daughter!

Here the Vetala asked: 'Tell me, King Vikramaditya, you who are renowned as the supreme judge of Bharatavarsha: what was the exact, lawful relationship of the child Priyadarshini to her own father, Prince Suryamukha? Resolve this genealogical knot, or your head will shatter into pieces!'

King Vikramaditya answered with judicial precision: 'According to the sacred Dharmashastras of Manu and Yajnavalkya, blood relationship is reckoned through direct biological descent, while civil relationships are determined by marriage. In civil and sacred law, Priyadarshini is first and foremost his legitimate daughter, for she was born of his own seed in lawful marriage. Yet through her mother's bloodline, she is simultaneously his first cousin once removed, being the grandchild of his paternal aunt! In the court of nature, she is his daughter; in the court of ancestral lineage, she is his cousin!'

'Your intellect cuts through the knot, O King!' chuckled the Vetala, and with a swift leap, he flew back to the tree.
moral: The tangled skein of human kinship sometimes weaves relationships that defy all simple definitions.
